ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a segment of a cubic function curve; the two labeled intercepts of the curve on the x-axis are (-1,0) and (1,0), and the labeled point near the y-axis is (0,2), indicating f(0)=2. Then reason: The problem gives f(x)=x^3+bx^2+cx+d, so the leading coefficient is 1, which is a monic cubic. From the x-intercepts on the figure, it can be known that -1 and 1 are roots, so one can set f(x)=(x+1)(x-1)(x-r), where r is the third root. Substitute the y-intercept f(0)=2, obtaining f(0)=(1)(-1)(-r)=r, so r=2. Therefore f(x)=(x+1)(x-1)(x-2)=(x^2-1)(x-2)=x^3-2x^2-x+2. Thus the coefficient b of x^2 is -2.
